questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```

## Verification Steps

**Local verification:**
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type sbom --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Check Rekor transparency log
rekor-cli get --uuid <rekor-uuid>
```

**CI verification:**
```bash
# In CI pipeline before deployment
cosign verify \
  --key pub.key \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/org/ML-platform/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?

Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design comprehensive CI/CD guardrails that ensure security, compliance, and data governance in a complex real-time analytics ecosystem. It tests cross-domain knowledge spanning container security, event streaming architecture, and policy-as-code implementation.

Key Concepts

- Container image security via cosign signing and registry allowlisting
- Data lineage tracking through Kafka topic metadata annotations
- Centralized policy enforcement using OPA/rego policies and Kyverno admission controllers
- Manifest-based validation with clear pass/fail criteria
- CI pipeline integration for automated policy verification

Code Example

```rego
# OPA policy example for Flink job validation
package flink.policy

deny[msg] {
    input.kind == "FlinkDeployment"
    not cosign_signed(input.spec.image)
    msg := "Flink job image must be cosign signed"
}

deny[msg] {
    input.kind == "KafkaTopic"
    not has_lineage_metadata(input.spec.config)
    msg := "Kafka topic must include lineage metadata"
}
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this architecture to support multi-cluster Kafka deployments?
- What strategies would you implement to monitor and remediate policy compliance drift over time?
- How would you handle emergency exemptions while maintaining audit trails?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical security controls: CI image signing, tag governance, and runtime enforcement with Kyverno; it requires understanding Cosign, Rekor, image verification, and policy-as-code interplay, plus how to craft minimal manifests and verify locally, in CI, and at runtime.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Tag policy regex
- Kyverno image verification at admission
- Minimal manifest testing (unsigned vs signed)
- CI and runtime integration and trade-offs (latency, private registries)

## Code Example

```yaml
# CI workflow snippet (Cosign verify)
name: CI Image Sign Check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          cosign verify registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signed-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validateImages:
      - image: "*"
        cosign:
          publicKey: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            ...
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment

  name: ride-service

  replicas: 2
```

```yaml
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0-signed
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to combine SBOM provenance, cryptographic attestation, and admission control in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments with concrete artifacts and workflow.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM provenance (CycloneDX)
- Cosign signatures and Rekor attestations
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy validation for image attestation and CVE severity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: ImageSBOMAttestation
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageSBOMAttestation
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package imagesbomattestation
      
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not valid_image(container.image)
        msg := sprintf("Container image %v fails SBOM/attestation validation", [container.image])
      }
      
      valid_image(image) {
        has_attestation(image)
        no_high_severity_vulns(image)
      }
```

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's practical understanding of security and governance gating for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). It tests knowledge of:

- Terraform IaC fundamentals and best practices
- Static analysis security scanning with tfsec
- Custom linting rules with tflint
- GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline configuration
- Secrets management best practices in CI environments

## Key Concepts

**tfsec**: A static analysis security scanner for Terraform code that detects hard-coded credentials, insecure configurations, and common infrastructure vulnerabilities before deployment. It scans for secrets embedded in code and flags misconfigurations that could lead to security breaches.

**tflint**: A extensible linter for Terraform that enforces organization-specific policies. It can be configured with custom rules to ensure consistency across infrastructure code, such as requiring standardized tags on all resources for billing, ownership tracking, and environment classification.

## What Success Looks Like

A strong answer demonstrates:
- Understanding of how tfsec catches secrets at scan time
- Knowledge of tflint's rule configuration for tag enforcement
- Familiarity with GitHub Secrets integration in CI/CD
- Ability to write practical, working Terraform configurations
- Awareness of local vs. CI validation workflows

This combination of skills is essential for maintaining secure, compliant infrastructure at scale.
